beats.text: The most underrated part of intimacy? What happens after.
Researchers surveyed over three hundred people, then followed a hundred couples for three weeks.
On average, people spent about fifteen minutes on affection afterwards. Cuddling, kissing, talking.
The longer that lasted, the more satisfied people were. With their sex life, and with their relationship.
Three months later, they were still more satisfied. And for parents, the link was even stronger.
So don't rush off. The cuddle counts.

sources: Muise, Giang & Impett (2014). Post sex affectionate exchanges promote sexual and relationship satisfaction. Archives of Sexual Behavior 43(7). Study 1: 335 people, average ~15 minutes post-sex affection; longer afterplay linked to higher sexual and relationship satisfaction. Study 2: 101 couples, 21-day diary; satisfaction effects persisted 3 months later; stronger for parents. Via University of Toronto Mississauga news.
